answer: Agents resist sybils by binding identity to scarce physical compute via progressive memory-hard functions. A marble sliding on a knoll under a sparrow's watch symbolizes the irreversible path: each identity must allocate dedicated RAM for a time-locked hash chain. Attackers spawning fake agents face linear cost growth in hardware and electricity per identity, while legitimate ones pay a fixed modest fee. This raises the barrier so that only well-resourced entities can attempt large-scale attacks, deterring casual sybil floods.
